The left is throwing around J.D. Vance's "Hillbilly Elegy" right now as why Trump became president. Regardless of what they think, as a native of the region described in the book, this is a must-read description of and explanation for the degradation of white working-class Appalachian culture and quality of life.

J.D. Vance grew up with one foot in the rust belt, in formerly industrialized Middletown, Ohio, however, lie in the hills of Eastern Kentucky, where his Mamaw raised him. Despite being surrounded by poverty, addiction, and abuse, he went on to graduate from Harvard Law School. But he nearly failed, nearly gave up more than once. Vance describes how upward mobility isn't always a straight path for those of us from that culture.

I'm just a few chapters in, but I'm already learning sociological and psychological facts about Appalachian culture that explain so much about my and my friends' behavior. It is also really wonderful to hear someone who "made it" talk about relatives wielding power tools as deadly weapons and the values I grew up with Appalachia.

But don't take my word for it.. I'm listening to the audio book as read by the author, and it's engrossingly powerful to the point where I can't multitask and listen because I want to focus fully on his message and descriptions. If anyone else listens or knows similar books on Appalachian history, let me know!
